chunks: He said: Abul Hasan Ali ibn Muhammad ibn al-Zubair al-Kufi reported to me, with permission to report from Abul Hasan Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Faddhal, who reported from Ali ibn Asbat, from Muhammad ibn Yahya the brother of Mughallas, from al-Ala ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from one of the two (Imams), peace be upon them, who said:
He said: I told him: "We see a man deeply engrossed in acts of devotion, humble and trying his best, yet he is opposed to you. Does that benefit him anything?"

Then he said: "O Muhammad, the similitude of us, the Ahlul Bayt, is like that of a household among the Banu Israel: whoever among them strived devotedly for forty nights, his supplication was answered. But a man among them strived for forty nights, then supplicated, and his prayer was not answered. So he came to Isa, son of Maryam, peace be upon him, complaining about his situation and asking him to pray for him. Isa purified himself, prayed, and then supplicated. Allah revealed to him: 'O Isa, indeed My servant came to Me through a gate other than the one through which I am reached. He called upon Me while his heart harbored doubt about you. Even if he were to call upon Me until his neck was severed and his fingers fell apart, I would not answer him.' Then Isa, peace be upon him, turned to him and said: 'You call upon your Lord while your heart doubts His Prophet?' He said: 'O Spirit of Allah and His Word, by Allah, it was indeed as you said. So ask Allah to remove it from me.' Then Isa, peace be upon him, prayed for him. Allah accepted it from him, and he was restored to the standing of his household."
Likewise, we the Ahlul Bayt -- Allah does not accept the deeds of a servant who doubts about us.

key_terms.أهل البيت: Ahlul Bayt — The People of the House; the Prophet Muhammad's household, specifically his daughter Fatimah, son-in-law Ali, and their progeny, the divinely appointed guides in Shia Islam.
key_terms.إجازة: Ijazah — Written authorization or permission to transmit hadith, a formal method of hadith transmission indicating scholarly trust.
key_terms.بني إسرائيل: Banu Israel — The Children of Israel; the Israelite nation, frequently referenced in the Quran and hadith as exemplary precedents.
key_terms.روح الله وكلمته: Ruh Allah wa Kalimatuh — Spirit of Allah and His Word; Quranic titles for Prophet Isa (Jesus), peace be upon him, reflecting his miraculous creation.

ai.seo_question: What happens to the worship of someone who doubts the Ahlul Bayt according to Imam al-Baqir or al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Amali of Sheikh al-Mufid addresses whether the worship of those who oppose the Ahlul Bayt (AS) benefits them. Muhammad ibn Muslim asks one of the two Imams (al-Baqir or al-Sadiq, peace be upon them) about a man who worships devoutly but opposes them. The Imam responds with a parable from Banu Israel: a household whose members' prayers were answered after forty nights of worship, except for one man whose prayers went unanswered because he harbored doubt about Prophet Isa (AS) in his heart. Allah revealed to Isa that this man approached Him through the wrong gate -- with doubt about His Prophet. Even if the man prayed until his neck was severed and his fingers fell apart, his prayers would not be answered. After Isa confronted the man and he confessed his doubt, Isa prayed for him, and Allah accepted it, restoring him to his household's standing. The Imam concludes: similarly, Allah does not accept the worship of one who doubts the Ahlul Bayt.
